title: Cellular: low latency and no stalls on a mobile network
description:
## Goal
phonepad stays responsive when the phone is on a cellular network: low glass-to-glass latency, no stalls, graceful quality loss when bandwidth drops. Today flow control allows 4 unacknowledged units, so at 150 ms RTT the stream is capped near 4/0.15 ≈ 26 units/s, every unit is CQP 24 regardless of link capacity, an IDR is ~40 KB, and the transport is WebSocket over TCP through tailscale serve (head-of-line blocking under loss, possible DERP relay).

## Operator decision
2026-11-09, verbatim: "One thing to consider is we should optimize the rendering for the latency, because I think I will be on the cell phone network, so we need to make sure that we handle this case. So this is a to-do. This is not that has to be done immediately. This is something that you should plan for. Feel free to file the beads, and I think you can start delegating to subagents this task when you feel ready." Earlier the same day: "be bold and experiment", "we can just fork and fix things", "address all gaps and limitations, accept all", "no legacy code". Approves: new dependencies, domain type and wire protocol changes, pad.html changes, transport changes. Nothing else; children inherit this.

## Children
Instrument first (every other child measures against it), then flow control, adaptive quality, keyframe smoothing, latency hiding on the phone, transport and path spikes.

## Oracle
All children closed; on the latency harness at emulated 150 ms RTT / 5 Mbit/s: ≥ 50 units/s while the pointer moves and capture→ack p95 ≤ RTT + 80 ms; operator judges it usable from a phone on cellular (human judgement, Iouri, on his phone).

title: Latency harness: per-stage timing and a network emulator
description:
## What
A measurement harness for latency under network conditions, usable by every other child:
- Each access unit carries an id and its capture time; the page reports per unit when it was received, decoded and drawn (in its ack or a separate report); the server computes per stage: capture→send, send→ack (network + decode), and units/s, bytes/s, stalls (> 250 ms with no drawn frame).
- A network emulator in front of the test instance (127.0.0.1:8766): configurable one-way delay, jitter, bandwidth cap and packet loss (TCP-level emulation in userspace is acceptable; netem needs root, which we don't use).
- `cargo xtask latency <profile>` runs the test instance + emulator + pointer mover + fake clients (fakeh264-style, or headless Chromium running the real page) and prints p50/p95/max per stage. Profiles at least: lan (0 ms), wifi (10 ms, 50 Mbit/s), lte (60 ms ±20, 10 Mbit/s), bad-lte (150 ms ±50, 3 Mbit/s, 1% loss).
## Oracle
- Known-case check (cm-27o): with the emulator set to added RTT D ∈ {0, 100, 200} ms, measured send→ack p50 rises by D ± 15 ms; with a 2 Mbit/s cap, measured bytes/s ≤ 2.1 Mbit/s.
- The printed table for all four profiles is recorded in the bead as the baseline for the other children.

title: Flow control sized to the link (RTT and delivery rate)
description:
## What
Flow control sized to the link instead of a fixed 4 units: the number of unacknowledged units/bytes a viewer may have adapts to the measured RTT and delivery rate (bandwidth-delay product), with a bound on queueing delay so latency doesn't build up. Keep the core invariants: a viewer never receives a delta without its reference; a stalled viewer never affects others; keyframe requests only when the viewer can take one. Lives in phonepad-core as a sum-type state machine with pure decide/evolve (cm-prk).
## Oracle
On the latency harness: lte profile ≥ 55 units/s and send→ack p95 ≤ RTT + 60 ms; bad-lte profile no stall > 500 ms in a 60 s run; lan profile unchanged from baseline (± 5%). Today (red): lte is capped near 4/RTT.

title: Adaptive quality: QP and rate follow delivered throughput
description:
## What
Adaptive quality: the encoder's per-unit quantizer (CQP allows per-frame QP) and, if needed, frame rate and output scale follow the delivered throughput, so the queue stays short on a slow link and quality returns when the link recovers. One encoder serves all viewers, so the policy must define what happens with viewers on different links (e.g. follow the slowest synced viewer, or per-viewer layers — choose and justify).
## Oracle
Harness with a 2 Mbit/s cap: send→ack p95 ≤ RTT + 100 ms and no stall > 500 ms; switch the cap to 20 Mbit/s mid-run: QP returns to its base within 5 s. Worst-frame PSNR at the base QP unchanged (h264-check). Today (red): at 2 Mbit/s the queue grows without bound or units are dropped en masse.

title: Keyframes without bursts on join and desync
description:
## What
Keyframes without bursts: a joining or desynced viewer today gets a ~40 KB IDR, which takes ~160 ms at 2 Mbit/s. Smooth this (e.g. periodic intra refresh / gradual decoder refresh instead of IDR on join, or a lower-QP IDR) while keeping "a viewer never receives a delta without its reference" true and verifiable.
## Oracle
Harness bad-lte: time from join to first drawn frame p95 ≤ 2×RTT + 150 ms; largest unit ≤ 3× median unit during steady state; h264-check still passes; WebCodecs on the phone (operator, Iouri) decodes it.

title: Latency hiding on the phone: predicted pointer and local pan
description:
## What
Latency hiding on the phone: pointer feedback must not wait for the network. The page moves the pointer ring immediately on touch (predicted from the moves it sent) and shifts the last drawn frame locally by the predicted pan, reconciling when the server's unit for that position arrives (units carry the cursor and region they were cropped at). Optionally the server sends a margin around the view so local pans reveal real pixels.
## Oracle
In the page (performance.now): touch→ring-redraw p95 ≤ 20 ms regardless of profile, measured on the harness with headless Chromium; on bad-lte the ring never jumps backwards more than 4 px at reconciliation; operator (Iouri) judges pointer feel on cellular acceptable.

title: Spike: transports better than WebSocket over TCP under loss
description:
## What
Spike, time box 1 day: transport alternatives to WebSocket-over-TCP through tailscale serve for cellular: WebTransport (HTTP/3, unreliable datagrams), WebRTC data channels or video track, a direct tailnet connection (not through `tailscale serve`) — what each costs in code, deps and the auth model (today: Tailscale-User-Login header from tailscale serve), and what it buys under loss.
## Oracle
A written comparison in this bead with measurements on the harness at bad-lte (1% loss): stall count and p95 send→draw for WebSocket vs the best alternative prototype; recommendation with the condition that would reverse it. The operator decides whether to adopt.

title: Spike: phone-to-desktop path on cellular (direct vs DERP)
description:
## What
Spike, time box 2 hours: the real path from the phone on cellular to the desktop. Is it direct or through a DERP relay (`tailscale status` shows "relay"), what RTT and bandwidth does it give (`tailscale ping`, iperf over the tailnet), and what makes it direct (UDP port mapping, router config, peer relay through a tagged node that already connects directly).
## Oracle
Measured RTT and throughput from the phone on cellular to the desktop recorded here, with path type; the harness profiles (child 1) adjusted to match; if relayed, a concrete step to get a direct path and its measured effect. Needs the operator's phone on cellular (Iouri runs the phone side).
